fields.agencyOffice: Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER)
fields.formName: Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report
fields.facility: Eastside 138 kV Substation; Energy Management System (EMS)

items.label: Criterion
items.value: Cyber event that causes interruptions of electrical system operations

items.label: Also met
items.value: Uncontrolled loss of 200 MW or more of firm system load for 15 minutes or more

items.label: Event type
items.value: Cyber event; physical equipment operated without authorization

items.label: Functional impact
items.value: Unauthorized control actions on two 138 kV breakers; EMS supervisory control unavailable while isolated

items.label: Attack vector
items.value: Under investigation; vendor remote access path to the EMS suspected

items.label: Level of intrusion
items.value: Control systems (EMS) and corporate network; no evidence yet in substation relays

items.label: Systems isolated
items.value: EMS servers and consoles disconnected from the corporate network at 15:11 EDT

items.label: Method
items.value: Manual breaker operation by field crews; substation in local control

items.label: Mutual assistance
items.value: Requested from Harbor County Electric for switching crews

fields.narrative:
At 14:52 EDT system operators observed open commands issued from the EMS to breakers 4 and 7 at the Eastside 138 kV substation that no operator had issued. 212 MW of load was lost. Operators moved the substation to local control at 15:05 and disconnected the EMS from the corporate network at 15:11. A field crew is closing breakers manually. Investigation is in progress; this report will be updated within 72 hours.

The vendor's remote support account was disabled at 15:14 EDT and its credentials are being rotated. The cooperative has engaged its incident response retainer. Customers are being restored by circuit priority, hospitals and water pumping first.
fields.status: Received. A confirmation has been sent to the submitter. Submit an updated report within 72 hours and a final report when the event is resolved.
